source.title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX

accepted.question_text: For each integer n at least 10, is the connected n-vertex graph with maximum irregularity always a pineapple graph PA(n,q), where a pineapple graph consists of a q-vertex clique together with an independent set on the remaining n−q vertices such that every vertex of the independent set is adjacent to one and the same clique vertex, and where the conjectured optimal clique size is q = ceil(n/2) + 1? Equivalently, does this specific pineapple maximize λ1(G) − d̄(G) over all connected graphs G on n vertices, where λ1(G) is the largest adjacency eigenvalue and d̄(G) is the average degree?

evidence.quote: The next section discusses the problem related to the irregularity of a graph... The following conjecture related to the irregularity of a graph have been formulated after some experiments with the system AGX.
Conjecture 2.1... The most irregular connected graph on n (n ≥ 10) vertices is a pineapple PA(n,q) in which the clique size q is equal to ⌈n/2⌉ +1.

accepted.question_text: For every connected graph G on n at least 3 vertices, is the spectral spread s(G) = λ1(G) − λn(G) always at most sqrt(4qn − 3q^2 − 2q + 1), where q = floor(2n/3) and λ1(G), λn(G) are the largest and smallest adjacency eigenvalues of G? Equivalently, is the maximum spectral spread among connected n-vertex graphs attained exactly by the complete split graph CS(n,q), meaning a graph consisting of a q-vertex clique and an independent set on the remaining n−q vertices with every clique vertex adjacent to every independent-set vertex, with independent-set size ceil(n/3)?

evidence.quote: The problem of finding the maximum value of s(G) among the class of connected graphs of given order n is an open problem. Experiments done with the AutoGraphiX system led to the following conjecture. Conjecture 3.1... Given n, the maximal value of the spectral spread of a graph on n vertices is obtained for a complete split graph CS(n,q) with an independent set of size n-q = ⌈n/3⌉.

Now, we reformulate Conjecture 3.1 in order to provide an upper bound in addition to extremal graphs. Conjecture 3.1’... Let G be a connected graph on n ≥ 3 vertices. Then s(G) ≤ sqrt(4 q n - 3 q^2 - 2 q + 1) with equality if and only if G is the complete split graph CS(n,q) with an independent set of size n-q = ⌈n/3⌉ and a clique of size q = ⌊2n/3⌋.

accepted.question_text: Is it true that every simple graph G on n vertices satisfies λ1(G) + λ1(Ḡ) ≤ (4/3)n − 5/3 minus the residue-class correction stated in the source, namely f1(n) when n mod 3 = 1, 0 when n mod 3 = 2, and f2(n) when n mod 3 = 0, where f1(n) = (3n − 2 − sqrt(9n^2 − 12n + 12))/6 and f2(n) = (3n − 1 − sqrt(9n^2 − 6n + 9))/6? If so, are the equality cases exactly the graphs G or complements Ḡ that are complete split graphs whose independent set has size floor(n/3), and also size ceil(n/3) when n mod 3 = 2?

evidence.page: Nordhaus–Gaddum inequality for the spectral radius, HTML lines 1208-1212
evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1... For any simple graph G, with complement Ḡ, index λ1(G) and n vertices we have λ1(G) + λ1(Ḡ) ≤ 4/3 n - 5/3 - { ... } ... This bound is sharp and attained if and only if G or Ḡ is a complete split graph with an independent set on ⌊n/3⌋ vertices (and also on ⌈n/3⌉ vertices if n mod(3) = 2).

accepted.question_text: Among all unicyclic graphs on n vertices, is the maximum graph energy achieved by the cycle Cn for n ≤ 7 and for n = 9, 10, 11, 13, 15, while for all remaining values of n the maximum is achieved by the lollipop graph Lol(n,6), obtained by joining a cycle C6 to a path P(n−6) with a single edge from a cycle vertex to an endpoint of the path?

evidence.page: Energy of a graph, HTML lines 1262-1268
evidence.quote: In this study, the particular case of unicyclic graphs was considered... The following conjecture was stated. Conjecture 5.2... Among unicyclic graphs on n vertices the cycle C_n has maximal energy if n ≤ 7 and n = 9, 10, 11, 13 and 15. For all other values of n the unicyclic graph with maximum energy is the lollipop Lol_{n,6}.

evidence.page: Energy of a graph, HTML lines 1279-1283
evidence.quote: Again, in another paper, Huo et al. (2011) solved completely the problem to get Theorem 5.5... Among all unicyclic graphs on n vertices, the cycle C_n has maximal energy if n ≤ 7 but n ≠ 4, and n = 9, 10, 11, 13 and 15; Lol_{4,3} has maximal energy if n = 4. For all other values of n, the unicyclic graph with maximal energy is Lol_{n,6}.

accepted.question_text: For n = 14 and for every n at least 16, is the bicyclic molecular graph of order n with maximum energy equal to P_n^{6;6}, where a molecular graph means a connected graph of maximum degree at most 4 and P_n^{6;6} is the graph formed from two 6-cycles and a path P(n−12) by joining one endpoint of the path to one cycle and the other endpoint to the other cycle by single edges?
accepted.context_brief: Maximum energy of bicyclic molecular graphs

evidence.page: Energy of a graph, HTML lines 1301-1305
evidence.quote: The problem of finding bicyclic graphs with maximum energy was also widely studied... they conjectured the following... recall that a molecular graph is a connected graph with maximum degree at most 4. Conjecture 5.9... For n = 14 and n ≥ 16, the bicyclic molecular graph of order n with maximal energy is ... represented by the graph P_n^{6;6} obtained from two copies of the cycle C_6 and a path P_{n-12} by attaching with an edge each endpoint of the path to one cycle.

evidence.page: Energy of a graph, HTML lines 1307-1311
evidence.quote: Li and Zhang (2007) gave a partial solution to the conjecture in the case of bipartite bicyclic graphs. The complete solution, in that case, was given by Huo et al. (2011). Theorem 5.10... Let G be any connected, bipartite bicyclic graph on n ≥ 12 vertices. Then E(G) ≤ E(P_n^{6;6}) with equality if and only if G ≡ P_n^{6;6}.

accepted.question_text: For every tricyclic graph G on n vertices with n = 20 or n at least 22, is the energy of G at most the energy of P_n^{6,6;6}, with equality only for P_n^{6,6;6}? Here P_n^{6,6;6} denotes the graph obtained from three copies of C6 and a path P(n−18) by adding a single edge from two of the 6-cycles to one endpoint of the path and a single edge from the third 6-cycle to the other endpoint.

evidence.page: Energy of a graph, HTML lines 1312-1319
evidence.quote: The problem of finding the tricyclic graphs maximizing the energy remains open... For n ≥ 22, we have a general conjecture obtained with AutoGraphiX. First let P_n^{6,6;6} denote the graph on n ≥ 20 obtained from three copies of C_6 and a path P_{n-18} by adding a single edge between each of two copies of C_6 to one endpoint of the path and a single edge from the third C_6 to the other endpoint of the P_{n-18}. Conjecture 5.11... Let G be a tricyclic graph on n vertices with n = 20 or n ≥ 22. Then E(G) ≤ E(P_n^{6,6;6}) with equality if and only if G ≡ P_n^{6,6;6}.

accepted.question_text: For every tetracyclic graph G on n vertices with n at least 26, is the energy of G at most the energy of P_n^{6,6;6,6}, with equality only for P_n^{6,6;6,6}? Here P_n^{6,6;6,6} denotes the graph obtained from four copies of C6 and a path P(n−24) by adding a single edge from two of the 6-cycles to one endpoint of the path and a single edge from the other two 6-cycles to the other endpoint.

evidence.page: Energy of a graph, HTML lines 1320-1326
evidence.quote: The problem of finding the quadricyclic (also called tetracyclic) graphs maximizing the energy remains open... For n ≥ 26, we have a general conjecture obtained with AutoGraphiX. First, let P_n^{6,6;6,6} denote the graph on n ≥ 26 obtained from four copies of C_6 and a path P_{n-24} by adding a single edge between each of two copies of C_6 to one endpoint of the path and a single edge from each of the two other copies of C_6 to the other endpoint of the P_{n-24}. Conjecture 5.12... Let G be a tetracyclic graph on n vertices with n ≥ 26. Then E(G) ≤ E(P_n^{6,6;6,6}) with equality if and only if G ≡ P_n^{6,6;6,6}.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Conjecture 5.13... Let r and n be positive integers such that n ≥ 6r + 4. Then E(G) ≤ E(P_n^{p × 6; q × 6}), where p = '⌊r/2⌉' and q = '⌊r/2⌋', with equality if and only if G ≡ P_n^{p×6; q×6}.

evidence.page: Energy of a graph, HTML lines 1327-1331
evidence.quote: Let p, q, r be integers such that r = p+q... Now the general conjecture is the following. Conjecture 5.13... Let r and n be positive integers such that n ≥ 6r + 4. Then E(G) ≤ E(P_n^{p × 6; q × 6}), where p = ⌊r/2⌉ and q = ⌊r/2⌋, with equality if and only if G ≡ P_n^{p×6; q×6}.
